objective: Replace pi-context's recursive interpretation of loosely typed Pi runtime internals with a typed, bounded context telemetry contract and simpler snapshot pipeline while preserving /pi-context, HUD adapter behavior, pressure notifications, content safety, and JSON/Markdown report compatibility.

in: Characterize authoritative aggregate usage, contributor estimates, pressure conversion, notifications, HUD adapter output, and Markdown/JSON report behavior.
Define a typed bounded context snapshot contract at the package-level service boundary.
Refactor pi-context to prefer authoritative telemetry and drastically reduce recursive contributor analysis.
Retain only bounded compatibility handling needed for supported current Pi runtime data.
Document the stable consumer contract for pi-hud initiative 03.
out: Changing /pi-context command names or removing JSON/Markdown report modes.
Capturing prompt, message, tool argument, file path, or other content in telemetry.
Refactoring pi-hud consumer code; initiative 03 owns that migration.
Adding a general arbitrary-object inspection framework.

constraints: Depends conceptually on the shared service conventions established by 01-pi-git-service-boundary, without duplicating its process domain.
Preserve /pi-context json through a typed system-JSON artifact operation.
Snapshots must remain bounded and content-safe and retain no prompt, message, tool-input, or path data.
Prefer authoritative aggregate usage; contributor detail must degrade explicitly rather than infer deeply from unknown object graphs.
Shared contracts/services must have no registration or UI side effects.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A typed bounded context telemetry contract replaces recursive interpretation as the primary snapshot input.
Contributor analysis is substantially simplified, bounded, and explicit about unavailable or degraded detail.
/pi-context, pressure notifications, HUD adapter values, and Markdown/JSON report naming and content remain compatible.
Tests prove snapshots retain no prompt, message, tool-input, or path content and remain bounded under malformed or oversized runtime data.
Focused and repository qualification passes and the supported consumer boundary is documented.

assessment.reason: The current implementation defensively traverses loosely typed runtime state; simplifying it affects privacy, compatibility, pressure signaling, reports, and a downstream HUD consumer.
unknowns: The installed Pi telemetry surface may not yet expose every desired contributor field.
Some contributor detail may require an explicit degraded mode until a native typed API is available.

practices.reason: Current outputs and prohibited-content guarantees must be explicit before replacing introspection.
The replacement must reduce complexity without reintroducing unsafe traversal in a compatibility layer.
Command, notification, report, and HUD-facing behavior require end-to-end confirmation.

obligations.text: Establish failing/passing characterization and privacy fixtures for aggregate usage, contributor degradation, pressure thresholds, notifications, HUD adapter output, report modes, malformed getters, cycles, and oversized data.
Verify the typed adapter is bounded, avoids recursive arbitrary-object interpretation, reports degraded contributor data explicitly, and never retains prohibited content.
Run context and HUD-focused tests plus typecheck, dependency, performance, command, and repository gates, then obtain independent review of privacy, compatibility, bounds, and contract clarity.

work.title: Characterize context telemetry, privacy, and compatibility behavior

testing.approach: Extend current tests with authoritative aggregates, contributor degradation, pressure/notification, report, HUD adapter, malformed-data, and prohibited-content cases before refactoring.
testing.reason: The current defensive implementation embodies implicit privacy and compatibility contracts that must not be lost.

work.title: Introduce the typed bounded telemetry contract and simplify snapshots

testing.approach: Implement the contract and bounded adapter, delete superseded recursive analysis, and run focused negative, privacy, and complexity-oriented review.
testing.reason: Typed authoritative data should replace defensive interpretation rather than merely wrap it.

evidence.summary: Source-bound self-review of src/contracts/context-telemetry.ts, src/services/context-telemetry.ts, the native adapter, and focused tests found no blocking issues. The shared service is registration-free and allowlist-sanitized; the native adapter reads only named supported properties, never enumerates or recursively traverses arbitrary values, caps every collection/text dimension, exposes degraded/unavailable contributor detail, and retains only numeric aggregates/fixed codes. Existing usage, pressure, contributor fields, HUD input, and report modes remain present; contributorDetail is additive. Focused typecheck and 20 tests pass; git diff --check is clean.

decisions.basis: The consolidation plan explicitly retains JSON through a typed system-artifact operation.

decisions.text: Prefer explicit contributor degradation over deep fallback introspection.
decisions.basis: The architecture defect is disproportionate complexity and sensitivity to undocumented runtime shapes.

risks.text: Native telemetry lacks contributor detail users currently see.
risks.mitigation: Preserve authoritative aggregate usage and expose bounded explicit degradation instead of guessing.
Use adversarial prohibited-content fixtures and source-bound privacy review.

risks.text: Report compatibility changes during service extraction.
